pr_title: ZipArchive now disposes given stream only once
pr_body:
Fixes #79695

Even though the `IDisposable` contract says that you should be able to call `Dispose` multiple times, be forgiving for implementations that throw when `Dispose` is called multiple times.

issue_context.title: ZipArchive disposes passed stream twice
issue_context.body:
### Description

I've tracked down a bug in our software where we had a stream which was not safe to call dispose multiple times (Fixed in the meantime =)). 
This surfaced when we passed said stream into a ZipArchive (reading only), because it is disposing the passed stream twice. 
I know that this is technically not a bug, but nonetheless something which can be improved.

The issue itself is caused by [this line](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.IO.Compression/src/System/IO/Compression/ZipArchive.cs#L167). The BinaryReader gets passed the stream, but the leaveOpen parameter is not set. Hence when [disposing](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.IO.Compression/src/System/IO/Compression/ZipArchive.cs#L464-L466) it disposes the stream twice.

### Reproduction Steps

- Create a erronous Stream implementation that has an issue when disposing twice.
- Create a ZipArchive in reading mode and dispose it

### Expected behavior

While not technically breaking, it still would be nice not to dispose things multiple times if not needed.

### Actual behavior

Disposes the input stream twice, once directly and once due to the BinaryReader.

### Regression?

not that I'm aware of

### Known Workarounds

Fix the wrongfully implemented stream :) 

### Configuration

I've tested it on .NET6, but it still exists on current main

### Other information

_No response_

> ### Expected behavior
> While not technically breaking, it still would be nice not to dispose things multiple times if not needed.

I don't believe this needs to be the case. For years and years, [Micosoft's official guidance has been](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/garbage-collection/implementing-dispose):
> To help ensure that resources are always cleaned up appropriately, a `Dispose` method should be idempotent, such that it is callable multiple times without throwing an exception. Furthermore, subsequent invocations of `Dispose` should do nothing.

There's probably several places in the BCL where `Dispose` could get called multiple times (perhaps no choice in the matter), so it's fair to make the implementer responsibile following the guidelines and not throw exceptions from `Dispose`.
Fully agree it doesn't need to be, but I think not doing something that is not needed is still better, even if not required. This is why I opened this issue.

review_comments: Do we have tests that validate the underlying Stream is closed when the ZipArchive is disposed according to leaveOpen?  This test being added isn't exercising leaveOpen.  Maybe it should be augmented to be a theory to control whether leaveOpen is false/true?
I have augmented the test to be a theory. It passes the leaveOpen parameter now explicitly and tests for the expected outcome. Thanks for your suggestion @stephentoub
